name: Corniche Garden Market
address: Sheraton Park, Al Corniche Street, West Bay, Doha
description: Doha’s biggest Saturday market, under the palms of Sheraton Park with forty growers.
about: What began as a handful of farm tables beside the Corniche is now the city’s busiest Saturday morning. Vegetable growers from the northern farms line the shaded paths, bakers and cheesemakers set up by the fountains, and the Wednesday evening edition is quieter — ideal for chatting to growers about next week’s harvest.

name: Al Gharrafa Garden Market
address: Al Gharrafa Park, Al Gharrafa Street, Al Gharrafa, Al Rayyan
description: A relaxed Friday-afternoon market of family farms, plant nurseries and home kitchens.
about: Friday afternoons in the park bring growers from Al Khor and Al Shamal with whatever was picked that morning. Expect crates of greenhouse tomatoes and cucumbers, bunches of herbs, seedlings for balcony gardens and a busy corner of home-made pickles.

name: Umm Salal Farm Market
address: Farm Road, Umm Salal Mohammed, Umm Salal
description: Straight from the surrounding farms: early Saturday picks and a lively Thursday evening.
about: Set among the farms north of the city, this market is where many growers sell first. Come early on Saturday for the best leafy greens and melons, or on Thursday evening when families stroll between the stalls once the heat has gone.

name: Al Sadd Family Market
address: Suhaim Bin Hamad Street, Al Sadd, Doha
description: A neighbourhood favourite for weekday evening shopping, close to home and easy to reach.
about: Twice a week a quiet car park turns into a small market street. Regulars come for local eggs, bread and seasonal vegetables on the way home, and children make straight for the juice stall.

name: Al Waab Organic Market
address: Al Waab Street, Al Waab, Doha
description: Certified-organic growers only, from hydroponic greens to farm eggs and raw honey.
about: Every stall here is run by an organic or pesticide-free grower. It is the best place in the city for salad leaves and herbs, and the honey table sells Sidr honey from local hives in autumn.

name: Souq Waqif Market Hall
description: A covered, air-cooled hall open every day — the reliable choice right through summer.
about: A permanent hall in the heart of the old souq with produce, dairy, dates and spice stalls under one roof. Because it is cooled and open daily, it is where most people shop between June and September, when outdoor markets take their summer break.

name: Al Rayyan Farmers Yard
address: Al Rayyan Al Jadeed Street, Al Rayyan
description: A friendly yard market with a children’s planting table and plenty of shade.
about: Run with a local school, the yard mixes farm stalls with a seedling swap and a planting table where children pot their own herbs to take home. Saturday mornings are the busiest.

name: Abu Hamour Fruit Market
address: Salwa Road service lane, Abu Hamour, Doha
description: Fruit by the crate: local dates, melons and citrus beside regional orchard fruit.
about: Growers and small importers share this long covered row. Local fruit takes pride of place — Khalas dates in late summer, melons in spring, citrus in winter — with orchard fruit brought in from the region the rest of the year.

name: Madinat Khalifa Dairy & Garden Market
description: Fresh laban, labneh and camel milk from local farms, plus herbs and plants.
about: Local dairy farms bring milk, laban, labneh and fresh cheeses twice a week, alongside a garden corner of herbs, seedlings and flowering plants. Bring a cool bag.

name: Al Wakrah Harbour Night Market
address: Al Wakrah Beach promenade, Al Wakrah
description: Lantern-lit evening stalls by the old harbour, with street food and late-night produce.
about: When the sun goes down the promenade fills with food stalls, fruit carts and growers selling the day’s pick. It is the best place for an evening out, and there is always sweet corn on the grill.

name: Katara Greenhouse Market
description: Under glass all year: hydroponic greens, herbs, microgreens and potted plants.
about: A cooled glasshouse hall where the city’s hydroponic growers sell leaves, herbs and microgreens harvested that morning. There are always potted herbs for the balcony and a café among the plants.

name: Old Airport Neighbourhood Market
address: Al Matar Street, Old Airport, Doha
description: A small, friendly market with Saturday story time for children and good family stalls.
about: Tucked behind the community centre, this is a market where the growers know most customers by name. Saturday mornings bring a story corner for children and home-baked bread.

name: Lusail Boulevard Market
description: Weekend evenings on the boulevard: growers, flowers and family-friendly food stalls.
about: The newest market in the guide takes over a stretch of the boulevard on Friday and Saturday evenings. Growers from the northern farms sit beside flower sellers and bakers, with plenty of space for pushchairs.

name: Porto Arabia Weekend Market
address: La Croisette, Porto Arabia, The Pearl-Qatar
description: A breezy waterfront market for organic produce, artisan bread and local honey.
about: Along the marina promenade on weekend mornings, a compact row of organic growers and artisan producers. Arrive early — the sourdough and strawberries are usually gone by ten.

name: Al Thumama Evening Market
address: Al Thumama Park, Al Thumama, Doha
description: Weekday evening market in the park, handy for after-work vegetables and eggs.
about: Two evenings a week the park’s lawn fills with growers and families. It is compact and easy to shop, with free parking and a play area beside the stalls.
